access_continuity_justification: The organization has three owners, fametrano, giacomocaironi and pmazzocchi, each an administrator of this repository and a reviewer of its publishing environments. If one becomes unavailable, the other two can still close issues, merge changes and release. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: btclib-node has no graphical or web interface: it is a headless node driven by command-line options and JSON-RPC. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/README.md
assurance_case_justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md states the threat model, the trust boundaries, the secure-design argument and the argument against common implementation weaknesses this criterion asks for. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
automated_integration_testing_justificat: test.yml runs the test suite on every pull request and every push to main that changes more than root Markdown files or the secrets baseline, and its aggregate job is a required check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml
build_non_recursive_justification: This tree builds no native binaries, so there is no recursive-build question to answer. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/pyproject.toml
build_preserve_debug_justification: No native build or installation step exists to strip or preserve debugging information. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/pyproject.toml
build_repeatable_justification: Every week sdist-rebuild.yml rebuilds the latest release's sdist from its tag. It passes only if the rebuilt file matches the release's attested digest byte for byte. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/.github/workflows/sdist-rebuild.yml
build_reproducible_justification: The sdist is built with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH from the commit. sdist-rebuild.yml rebuilds the latest release's sdist from its tag and verifies it against the release's attestation, and RELEASING.md gives the same check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/.github/workflows/sdist-rebuild.yml
build_standard_variables_justification: This tree builds no native binaries -- it is pure Python on the uv_build backend -- so there is no compiler or linker invocation for CC/CFLAGS/LDFLAGS to reach. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/pyproject.toml
bus_factor_justification: fametrano wrote almost all of the code and is the only person who knows it in depth. The claude account in the contributors graph comes from the Co-Authored-By trailer on AI-assisted commits, almost all of them fametrano's. pmazzocchi, an organization owner, did the 2026-09-30 security review and has since made ten commits, from 2026-10-15 to 2026-10-26. In the last year, outside contributors have made only small changes. giacomocaironi, also an organization owner, wrote early parts of the code but has made no commit since 2023. The organization owners administer every repository. Knowledge of the code rests on fametrano alone. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/graphs/contributors
code_of_conduct_justification: btclib-org/.github's CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md is this repository's code of conduct, through GitHub's organization-wide default; the community-profile API reports it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
code_review_standards_justification: REVIEWING.md states what a review checks, how a finding is written and what clears a pull request; the part shared by every repository is followed by what this tree checks in particular. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/REVIEWING.md
coding_standards_enforced_justification: ruff-check, ruff-format and mypy run as pre-commit hooks, and lint.yml runs the same .pre-commit-config.yaml in CI as a required check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml
coding_standards_justification: pyproject.toml selects every ruff rule (select = ["ALL"]) with a documented ignore list, and runs mypy in strict mode. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/pyproject.toml
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states the coding-standard, lint-gate and 100%-coverage requirements a contribution must meet before it can land. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contributors_unassociated_justification: fametrano is the only significant contributor. In the last year, outside contributors have made only small changes. pmazzocchi, an organization owner, has made ten commits, from 2026-10-15 to 2026-10-26; pmazzocchi and fametrano are associated: both are CheckSig co-founders, as their GitHub profiles state. giacomocaironi, also an organization owner, wrote early parts of the code but has made no commit since 2023. https://github.com/fametrano https://github.com/pmazzocchi
copyright_per_file_justification: Every source file under src/ opens with "Copyright (c) The btclib developers", e.g. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/src/btclib_node/__init__.py
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: A node validates what the consensus rules define, and Bitcoin's consensus rules fix secp256k1, SHA-256 and the signature schemes. Another algorithm needs a soft fork first, and the project follows one when it activates. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/README.md
crypto_call_justification: The node reimplements no cryptography: it calls btclib, ecc and Python's hashlib and hmac.
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: btclib-node's p2p transport is not TLS-based (Bitcoin's wire protocol has no TLS layer), so there is no TLS support for this criterion to apply to. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md
crypto_credential_agility_justification: The RPC credentials are the cookie file and the -rpcauth entries, kept apart from the rest of the configuration and replaced without recompiling. The node holds no long-term private key. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/SECURITY.md
crypto_keylength_justification: BIP324 fixes the key lengths: a secp256k1 key, about 128 bits of security, and 256-bit ChaCha20 keys, above NIST's 112-bit floor for 2030. No shorter key can be configured. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/src/btclib_node/p2p/v2transport.py https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/src/btclib/p2p/bip324.py
crypto_password_storage_justification: -rpcauth credentials belong to the node's operator and the operator's own RPC clients, not to external users of a service. The node stores them as Bitcoin Core does, a salted single-round HMAC-SHA256, as the docstring of rpc/auth.py records. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/src/btclib_node/rpc/auth.py
crypto_pfs_justification: Each v2 connection draws a fresh secp256k1 key from secrets, and BIP324 derives the session keys from an ElligatorSwift ECDH over it, so a later key compromise exposes no past session. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/src/btclib_node/p2p/v2transport.py
crypto_published_justification: The node implements no algorithm of its own: it calls btclib and ecc, which implement published algorithms, and Python's hashlib and hmac.
crypto_random_justification: The BIP324 ephemeral keys, the RPC cookie and salts, and the P2P nonces come from Python's secrets module. Every other random value comes from the OS CSPRNG, through SystemRandom or os.urandom. Cluster linearization alone expands such a seed with Core's non-cryptographic xoroshiro128++, as Core does. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/tree/main/src/btclib_node
crypto_tls12_justification: btclib-node's p2p transport is not TLS-based (Bitcoin's wire protocol has no TLS layer), so there is no TLS support for this criterion to apply to. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md
crypto_used_network_justification: Peer traffic uses BIP324's encrypted v2 transport by default. Plaintext v1 is on only when started with -v1transport=1 or -v2transport=0. The JSON-RPC listener speaks plain HTTP only, with no TLS option. It binds loopback by default. Peers are found through DNS seeds over plain DNS, as in Bitcoin Core. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/SECURITY.md#where-this-node-departs-from-bitcoin-core https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/SECURITY.md#limitations-not-vulnerabilities
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: btclib-node's p2p transport is not TLS-based (Bitcoin's wire protocol has no TLS layer), so there is no TLS support for this criterion to apply to. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No SHA-1 or MD5 appears under src/. The node uses the algorithms Bitcoin and BIP324 fix: secp256k1, SHA-256 and ChaCha20-Poly1305. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/SECURITY.md
dco_justification: main requires the lint / Sign-off check, which refuses a pull request with a commit that lacks its author's Signed-off-by: trailer. Dependabot's, pre-commit.ci's and claude[bot]'s commits are exempt. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/scripts/check_sign_off.py
delivery_mitm_justification: Distribution channels (GitHub, PyPI) use HTTPS exclusively.
delivery_unsigned_justification: Releases are published to PyPI and GitHub Releases and installed with pip from PyPI, all over HTTPS. No package or hash is fetched over plain HTTP. https://pypi.org/project/btclib-node/ https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/releases
dependency_monitoring_justification: Dependabot version updates cover uv and github-actions, and Dependabot security updates are on. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml
description_good_justification: btclib-node is a full bitcoin node written in Python and based on btclib. It is alpha software. https://btclib.org/btclib-node/
discussion_justification: GitHub supports discussions on issues and pull requests.
documentation_achievements_justification: README.md shows the OpenSSF Scorecard, Best Practices and Baseline badges together. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/README.md
documentation_architecture_justification: ARCHITECTURE.md documents the node's loop, its protocol and RPC surface, the transport, the chain state and store, validation, and what is delegated to btclib. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md
documentation_current_justification: The docs build is a required check (docs.yml, -W -n), and tests/unit/docs_test.py fails when a shipped module has no API page. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/.github/workflows/docs.yml
documentation_quick_start_justification: docs/source/running_a_node.md's Starting a node gives the install command and the command for each chain, and README.md links it. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/docs/source/running_a_node.md
documentation_roadmap_justification: ROADMAP.md, organization-wide in btclib-org/.github, is reviewed every September and states what is maintained, what is intended and what is deliberately not. This repository's README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md link it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/ROADMAP.md
documentation_security_justification: SECURITY.md's Limitations section lists what the node does not protect against: RPC credentials sent as plain HTTP, BIP324's lack of peer authentication, and the Alpha status. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/SECURITY.md
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The suite and the fuzz harnesses run without -O, so Python assert statements are active. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/.github/workflows/fuzz.yml
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No fuzzing or mutation-testing finding is open, and the weekly fuzz and mutation runs on main pass. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/actions/workflows/fuzz.yml https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/actions/workflows/mutation.yml
dynamic_analysis_justification: Every release runs the test suite before it is published. release.yml calls test.yml, and the PyPI upload runs only if it passes. The suite fails below 100% coverage, branches included. Atheris fuzzing and cosmic-ray mutation testing also run every week. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/.github/workflows/fuzz.yml
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: This tree ships pure Python, a memory-safe language; it produces no software written in a memory-unsafe language for a dynamic memory-safety tool to run against. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/pyproject.toml
external_dependencies_justification: Every dependency is declared in machine-readable form in pyproject.toml's [project.dependencies] and dependency-groups, resolved and pinned in the committed uv.lock. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/pyproject.toml
floss_license_justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).
floss_license_osi_justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).
governance_justification: GOVERNANCE.md, organization-wide in btclib-org/.github, documents the decision model and every role a contributor, reviewer or owner holds; this tree's README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md link it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
hardened_site_justification: The project site is served over HTTPS with Content-Security-Policy (frame-ancestors 'none'), X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and Strict-Transport-Security. https://btclib.org/btclib-node/ The repository on github.com sends all four. PyPI's project page https://pypi.org/project/btclib-node/ sends all but the CSP; that is PyPI's to set. The documentation site https://btclib-node.readthedocs.io/ is served by Read the Docs over HTTPS with Strict-Transport-Security and X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, and no Content-Security-Policy or X-Frame-Options; that is Read the Docs' to set. Measured with curl -sIL on 2026-11-12.
hardening_justification: ruff's select = ["ALL"] includes the bandit S rules, so a hardening defect such as unsafe deserialization or shell injection fails the lint gate. CodeQL also runs on every pull request and every push to main. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml
implement_secure_design_justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md's Secure design principles argues how each principle is applied, and its Trust boundaries covers the JSON-RPC listener and peer input. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
input_validation_justification: Peer input is checked at the transport before a handler sees it: a v1 header's length and magic, a v2 packet's length and authentication. Every block is checked against the consensus rules before it is accepted. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
installation_common_justification: The package is on PyPI, so `pip install btclib-node` (or `pip uninstall`) is the commonly-used convention for installing and removing it; README.md gives the exact command. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/README.md
installation_development_quick_justifica: `uv sync` installs the whole development environment in one command; CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* section gives it beside `uv run pytest` and the lint gate. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
installation_standard_variables_justific: Installation is `pip install`, which follows pip's and the interpreter's own install-location conventions; there is no project-specific installer that could diverge from that convention. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/pyproject.toml
interfaces_current_justification: ruff's UP and FA rules flag deprecated constructs, and pytest turns every deprecation warning into an error. deps-latest and deps-oldest run the suite weekly at the newest and the floor versions. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/pyproject.toml
internationalization_justification: btclib-node generates no end-user text and sorts no human-readable strings; its output (hex, addresses, RPC results, log lines) is technical data. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/README.md
know_common_errors_justification: The primary developer wrote ASSURANCE_CASE.md's Common implementation weaknesses, which names each weakness and what counters it. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
know_secure_design_justification: The primary developer wrote ASSURANCE_CASE.md's Secure design principles, which argues how each is applied here. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
license_per_file_justification: Every source file under src/ states "Distributed under the MIT software license", e.g. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/src/btclib_node/__init__.py
maintenance_or_update_justification: Only the latest release is supported and nothing is backported (SECURITY.md). RELEASING.md runs griffe check against the previous tag, and RELEASE_NOTES.md lists what a user must act on to upgrade. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md
osps_ac_01_01_justification: The btclib-org organization requires two-factor authentication of every member and accepts only secure methods, not SMS. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/1362#issuecomment-5903994882
osps_ac_02_01_justification: A new member gets read access, the organization's base permission (gh api orgs/btclib-org --jq .default_repository_permission). Every higher grant is assigned by hand, through an issue in btclib-org/.github that an owner other than the one asking approves. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#how-a-decision-is-made
osps_ac_03_01_justification: The main-self-merge ruleset requires a pull request for every change to main. Its one bypass actor, fametrano, holds it in pull_request mode, which excuses the approval but still refuses a direct push, so nobody pushes to main directly. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/2021
osps_ac_03_02_justification: The main-integrity ruleset forbids deleting main and has no bypass actor. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets
osps_ac_04_01_justification: The default GITHUB_TOKEN is read-only at the organization and the repository, and cannot approve pull requests. Every workflow also sets permissions: contents: read at the top. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning
osps_ac_04_02_justification: Every workflow sets permissions: contents: read at the top, and a job adds a write scope only where it uses it. zizmor's excessive-permissions audit runs in the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#what-every-workflow-does
osps_br_01_01_justification: No workflow uses pull_request_target or workflow_run. Event fields and inputs reach run: steps only through env:, and zizmor's template-injection audit in the required lint check refuses the unsafe form. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml
osps_br_01_03_justification: Pull-request runs use the pull_request and pull_request_review_comment triggers, which give a fork no secrets and a read-only token. The review job, which holds a secret, runs only when the head repository is this one. On issue_comment, the mention job, which holds a secret on any pull request, checks out the default branch. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/workflows/reusable-claude-review.yml
osps_br_01_04_justification: The only workflow_dispatch input is verified-signatures.yml's before and after, which the called workflow reads through env: and refuses unless they are commit shas. A release tag's name is checked against the package version before anything is built. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml
osps_br_02_01_justification: Each release has a unique calendar version (YYYY.M.D), set by a signed v* tag. release.yml refuses a tag that disagrees with the package version or is not on main, and PyPI never accepts a version twice. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/releases
osps_br_02_02_justification: Every release asset carries the version in its file name: the sdist, the wheel, the CycloneDX SBOM and the attestation bundle. The attestation binds each asset to its digest. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/releases/latest
osps_br_03_01_justification: Every official channel the project lists is served over HTTPS only: the GitHub repository, its issue tracker and advisories, and the documentation at https://btclib-node.readthedocs.io.
osps_br_03_02_justification: Releases are distributed through PyPI and GitHub Releases, both HTTPS only. PyPI files carry PEP 740 attestations and the GitHub release a Sigstore bundle. https://pypi.org/project/btclib-node/
osps_br_04_01_justification: The GitHub release body is RELEASE_NOTES.md's entry: what a user must act on, breaking and security changes included. CHANGELOG.md lists every change. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md
osps_br_05_01_justification: Python dependencies come from PyPI, and the required test check runs the suite with uv from the committed uv.lock with --locked. pre-commit installs its hooks at the revisions .pre-commit-config.yaml names. Third-party actions are pinned by commit SHA. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#uvlock
osps_br_06_01_justification: Every PyPI file carries a PEP 740 attestation from Trusted Publishing. The GitHub release carries a Sigstore build-provenance bundle over each asset's SHA-256. The tag is signed. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/releases/latest
osps_br_07_01_justification: Secret scanning and push protection are on, so a push carrying a recognised credential is refused. The detect-private-key and detect-secrets hooks run in the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/.secrets.baseline
osps_br_07_02_justification: A secret is an environment secret that only the owners reach. A secret kept in any other store is recorded in the REPOSITORY.md of the repository that uses it, and btclib-org/.github's tests/secrets_test.py refuses an unrecorded one. A secret is rotated when an owner changes or an exposure is suspected. The secrets kept outside an environment are rotated before they are a year old, and the list is reviewed yearly. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning
osps_do_01_01_justification: The user documentation is docs/source/running_a_node.md, which README.md links, and the API reference at https://btclib-node.readthedocs.io/.
osps_do_02_01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md says where a defect is filed, and the bug-report form asks for what a report needs. SECURITY.md sends a vulnerability to a private channel instead. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml
osps_do_03_01_justification: SECURITY.md gives the gh attestation verify command for the release assets, and RELEASING.md the check that rebuilds the sdist from its tag. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_do_03_02_justification: The verify command pins the signer and the source: --owner btclib-org, --signer-workflow the organization's reusable-build.yml (reusable-attest.yml for v2026.9.24, release.yml before it) and --source-ref the release tag, and it compares the certificate's sourceRepositoryIdentifier with this repository's id, which a rename keeps. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_do_04_01_justification: SECURITY.md's *Supported versions*: only the latest release is supported, a fix ships as a new release, and nothing is backported. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_do_05_01_justification: SECURITY.md: only the latest release is supported, so a release stops receiving security updates when the next one is published. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_do_06_01_justification: pyproject.toml gives the reason for each runtime dependency. uv obtains them from PyPI and pins them in uv.lock, and Dependabot tracks them weekly with a seven-day cooldown. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#dependabot-and-pre-commitci
osps_do_07_01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md gives the build: uv is the only prerequisite, uv sync builds the environment from uv.lock, and uv build produces the sdist and wheel. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_gv_01_01_justification: btclib-org/.github's GOVERNANCE.md, *Roles*, names who holds access to sensitive resources. fametrano is the maintainer. Every owner, named there by login, is an administrator of every repository and a reviewer of the publishing environments. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
osps_gv_01_02_justification: btclib-org/.github's GOVERNANCE.md, *Roles*, describes the maintainer, owners, repository collaborators, contributors, reviewers, the review bot, Dependabot and pre-commit.ci, and what each owes. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
osps_gv_02_01_justification: Proposed changes and usage obstacles are discussed publicly in the repository's GitHub issues (with a question form) and pull requests; cross-repository questions go to btclib-org/.github's tracker. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/issues
osps_gv_03_01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains the contribution process: one subject per pull request, the local gates, the review and the landing. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_gv_03_02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states what a contribution must meet: one subject, a Signed-off-by trailer on every commit, the gates CI runs, 100% line and branch coverage, and a review against REVIEWING.md. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_gv_04_01_justification: A grant of write or admin, to any repository of the organization, is an issue in btclib-org/.github that states the reason, and an owner other than the one asking approves it there. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#how-a-decision-is-made
osps_le_01_01_justification: main requires the lint / Sign-off check, which refuses a commit that lacks its author's Signed-off-by: trailer, Dependabot's, pre-commit.ci's and claude[bot]'s aside. Web commits are signed off automatically. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/scripts/check_sign_off.py
osps_le_02_01_justification: The source code is under the MIT license, which the OSI approves. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_le_02_02_justification: The released wheels and sdist declare License-Expression: MIT, the same OSI-approved license as the source. https://pypi.org/project/btclib-node/
osps_le_03_01_justification: The license text is the repository's root LICENSE file. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_le_03_02_justification: The LICENSE file ships inside every release asset: the sdist root and the wheel's .dist-info/licenses/. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_qa_01_01_justification: The repository is public on GitHub at a static URL. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node
osps_qa_01_02_justification: Git history on GitHub records every change with its author, committer, date and signature; linear history and no force-pushes on main keep that record from being rewritten. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/commits/main
osps_qa_02_01_justification: pyproject.toml declares the direct dependencies ([project] dependencies, optional extras and dependency groups), and the committed uv.lock resolves and pins them. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/pyproject.toml
osps_qa_02_02_justification: Every release attaches a CycloneDX 1.6 SBOM generated from the built wheel, listing its dependencies and covered by the release attestation. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/releases/latest
osps_qa_03_01_justification: main's branch protection requires every CI status check that REPOSITORY.md's Required checks on main names. enforce_admins is off, so an admin merge without them is a manual bypass, which the control allows. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/REPOSITORY.md#required-checks-on-main https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets
osps_qa_04_01_justification: The organization standard's section 2 (*Which repositories, and how far*) lists every repository of btclib-org and its tier, and the organization profile lists the published packages. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#which-repositories-and-how-far
osps_qa_04_02_justification: Each release is built from this single repository; the sibling packages it depends on are released separately from their own repositories, which are held to the same standard. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node
osps_qa_05_01_justification: No generated executable is committed. The binary files are fuzz seed inputs, compressed block and header test vectors under tests/unit/chainstate/_data, and the Sphinx inventory python.inv. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/tests/_data/README.md
osps_qa_05_02_justification: None of the binary files is code. tests/_data/README.md gives the upstream repository and commit of each bz2 and zst test vector, which vendored-vectors.yml re-checks weekly, and how the xz header files were derived, whose sha256 the tests pin. The others are fuzz seed inputs and docs/source/_inventories/python.inv. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/tests/_data/README.md
osps_qa_06_01_justification: test.yml's aggregate check ('test: every job passed') is a required status check on main. It runs the test suite on every pull request that changes more than root prose or the secrets baseline, and reports a pull request changing only those as a pass. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml
osps_qa_06_02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* gives the command that runs the suite and which workflows run it on every pull request, on main and on a schedule, and which of them gate a merge. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_qa_06_03_justification: The policy is 100% line and branch coverage (CONTRIBUTING.md, standard section 8). pyproject.toml sets fail_under = 100, so untested new code fails the required test check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/pyproject.toml
osps_qa_07_01_justification: The main-self-merge ruleset requires one approving review from somebody other than the author before a merge to main, and dismisses an approval on a new push. Its bypass list holds one actor, fametrano, in pull_request mode, at rest: the organization-wide bypass the maintainer kept on 2026-11-04 (btclib-org/.github#2021 and btclib-org/.github#2040). Read with gh api repos/btclib-org/btclib-node/rulesets/20736359 --jq '{name, bypass: [.bypass_actors[] | {actor_id, bypass_mode}], reviews: (.rules[] | select(.type == "pull_request") | .parameters | {required_approving_review_count, dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push})}', with admin rights, on 2026-11-12; actor 3296421 is fametrano (gh api users/fametrano --jq .id). GOVERNANCE.md has the maintainer add that bypass back only in an emergency, and records that it stands until the backlog settles. It is used for ordinary work: over the last two releases, 83 of the 88 pull requests merged had no approval from anybody other than their author (v2026.11.12 5 of 7, v2026.11.11 78 of 81). Each count is merged minus approved. Counted with gh pr list -R btclib-org/btclib-node -s merged -L 500 -S 'merged:2026-11-12T00:28:10Z..2026-11-12T08:36:22Z' --json author,reviews -q '[.[] | .author.login as $a | [.reviews[] | select(.state == "APPROVED" and .author.login != $a) | .author.login] | unique] | {merged: length, approved: map(select(length > 0)) | length, approvers: (add | unique)}' for v2026.11.12, and the same command over merged:2026-11-07T01:53:14Z..2026-11-12T00:28:09Z for v2026.11.11. The ruleset's version in force for both windows, 55767402 of 2026-11-01, the newest in gh api repos/btclib-org/btclib-node/rulesets/20736359/history, requires that approval and holds that bypass, read with history/55767402 (with admin rights), so each of the 83 merged through the bypass; fametrano merged all 83, counted with gh pr list -R btclib-org/btclib-node -s merged -L 500 -S 'merged:2026-11-07T01:53:14Z..2026-11-12T08:36:22Z' --json author,reviews,mergedBy -q '[.[] | .author.login as $a | select(any(.reviews[]; .state == "APPROVED" and .author.login != $a) | not) | .mergedBy.login] | group_by(.) | map("\(.[0]) \(length)")'. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#how-a-decision-is-made
osps_sa_01_01_justification: ARCHITECTURE.md describes each component and how it reaches outside the process: the node's main loop, the peer-to-peer protocol and the RPC surface, the transport, the chain state and its store, and validation. ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Threat model* and *Trust boundaries* name the actors and what each can do. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
osps_sa_02_01_justification: The API reference is generated from the docstrings of every public module, and tests/unit/docs_test.py fails when a shipped module is missing from it. https://btclib-node.readthedocs.io/
osps_sa_03_01_justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md is the security assessment: what is claimed, the threat model, the trust boundaries and how each common implementation weakness is countered; SECURITY.md's limitations section records the known residual risks. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
osps_sa_03_02_justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Threat model* names the assets, adversaries and what is not defended, and *Trust boundaries* maps the attack surface where untrusted input enters, each argument naming the file, test or workflow behind it. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
osps_vm_01_01_justification: SECURITY.md's *Reporting a vulnerability* gives the private channels, a GitHub security advisory or email, and the timeframes: a report is acknowledged within 7 days, and a fix or a published advisory follows within 90 days. A report triaged as easy to rediscover is fixed as soon as possible, and its advisory is published with the fix. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability
osps_vm_02_01_justification: SECURITY.md names the security contacts: a private GitHub security advisory, or email to security at btclib dot org. btclib-org/.github's GOVERNANCE.md, *Roles*, says that address reaches every organization owner. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
osps_vm_03_01_justification: Private vulnerability reporting is enabled, and SECURITY.md points to it (the Security tab's 'Report a vulnerability') and gives an email address as the alternative. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/security/advisories/new
osps_vm_04_01_justification: Vulnerabilities are published as GitHub security advisories on this repository, each naming the release that fixes it. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/security/advisories
osps_vm_04_02_justification: The CycloneDX SBOM a release attaches lists, in its vulnerabilities array, every vulnerability that the tree's .github/vex.toml judges not to affect the release, with the reason. A tree with no such judgement has no vex.toml, and its SBOM has no vulnerabilities key. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#12-releasing
osps_vm_05_01_justification: The standard sets the threshold: actions/dependency-review-action fails a pull request that adds or changes a dependency with an advisory of moderate severity or above, or with a licence outside the allow-list. Its settings are one file, btclib-org/.github's .github/dependency-review.yml. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/dependency-review.yml https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning
osps_vm_05_02_justification: release.yml runs uv audit over every dependency the wheel declares, and every publish job needs it to succeed. An advisory, or a service it cannot reach, stops the release. The only exemption is an id that the tree's own .github/vex.toml, carried into the release's signed SBOM, states as not affecting it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#12-releasing
osps_vm_05_03_justification: The required lint check audits the whole uv.lock, every dependency group, on every pull request: check_audit.py --all-groups runs uv audit, which reads OSV's malicious-package (MAL-) entries as well as advisories. Any such entry fails the check, and so does an OSV that cannot be reached. The audit's only exemption is a .github/vex.toml entry, reviewed like any other change. The required Dependency review check also blocks a change that adds a dependency with an advisory of moderate severity or above, or a licence outside the allow-list. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#12-releasing https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning
osps_vm_06_01_justification: The standard's section 5 sets a threshold of zero for ruff: select = ALL, bandit's S rules included, and each finding is fixed or suppressed in place with a reason. zizmor holds workflows to the same, in the required lint check. CodeQL runs on every pull request, but the standard sets no threshold for its alerts. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#5-ruff
osps_vm_06_02_justification: The required lint check runs .pre-commit-config.yaml on every pull request (ruff with the S rules, strict mypy, zizmor, detect-secrets) and blocks the merge on any finding not suppressed in place with a reason. CodeQL also runs on every pull request but is not a required check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/.github/workflows/lint.yml
regression_tests_added50_justification: A merged pull request that changes code under src/ also changes tests/, unless it leaves behaviour as it was (a docstring, a comment, a move, a removal, a refactor or a speed-up) or a test already in the suite fails without it. The 100% line and branch coverage gate also fails a fix whose new code no test runs. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-environment-and-the-gates
release_notes_vulns_justification: The GitHub release notes name each advisory the release fixes: v2026.10.8's name GHSA-74pj-5cgg-3m66, and v2026.10.4's name GHSA-rm5x-6v45-j8m6, GHSA-6hv4-mmgr-39wq and GHSA-68jv-ghr4-jjmj. RELEASE_NOTES.md's v2026.10.4 section does not name those three. No later release fixes a published advisory; v2026.11.2 and v2026.11.4 list their security fixes under a Security heading, such as the drop of a peer paused on a full send buffer (closes #2112), the defect of Bitcoin Core's 2026-10-28 disclosure. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/releases/tag/v2026.10.4 https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/releases/tag/v2026.11.4
repo_distributed_justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git is distributed.
repo_interim_justification: development is on the main branch of https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node
repo_public_justification: Repository on GitHub, which provides public git repositories with URLs.
repo_track_justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git can track the changes, who made them, and when they were made.
report_process_justification: Bugs are reported in GitHub Issues, through the bug-report form. CONTRIBUTING.md's The issue tracker says where, and SECURITY.md takes vulnerabilities instead. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/issues https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-issue-tracker
report_tracker_justification: Each repository uses its own GitHub Issues tracker for individual issues, with issue forms under .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/, and an organization-wide tracker in btclib-org/.github for cross-repository findings. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/issues
require_2FA_justification: The btclib-org organization requires two-factor authentication of every member. https://github.com/btclib-org
roles_responsibilities_justification: btclib-org/.github's GOVERNANCE.md, *Roles*, names the maintainer, the owners, repository collaborators, contributors, reviewers, the review bot, Dependabot and pre-commit.ci, and what each owes. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
secure_2FA_justification: The btclib-org organization requires two-factor authentication and allows only secure methods: TOTP apps, security keys or passkeys, and GitHub Mobile, not SMS. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/1362#issuecomment-5903994882
security_review_justification: pmazzocchi, an owner other than the maintainer, reviewed the project on 2026-09-30. The review pins its scope to a commit, checks each claim of ASSURANCE_CASE.md, states what it did not cover and files each finding as an issue. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/issues/1559
signed_releases_justification: Every PyPI file carries a PEP 740 attestation from Trusted Publishing, and each GitHub release a Sigstore provenance bundle. SECURITY.md gives the gh attestation verify command. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/releases/latest
sites_password_security_justification: Project sites are GitHub, PyPI and Read the Docs; this repository runs no site of its own that stores user passwords. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/SECURITY.md
small_tasks_justification: Small tasks for new contributors carry the label "good first issue", which CONTRIBUTING.md sets aside for a first contribution. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/issues?q=label%3A%22good+first+issue%22
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL's python analysis (codeql.yml) runs on a schedule, on every pull request and on every push to main, and ruff's `select = ["ALL"]` includes the bandit-derived S rules. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml
static_analysis_fixed_justification: No code-scanning alert is open: gh api --paginate 'repos/btclib-org/btclib-node/code-scanning/alerts?state=open' --jq '.[] | "\(.number) \(.most_recent_instance.location.path)"' prints nothing. An alert in test code that is not fixed is dismissed as "used in tests", with the reason btclib-org/btclib-node#1258 gives: the test holds or probes a port on every interface, so that the node's own every-interface bind or probe sees it taken. Alert 108 is one of them (btclib-org/btclib-node#2427). Listed with gh api --paginate 'repos/btclib-org/btclib-node/code-scanning/alerts?state=dismissed' --jq '.[] | select(.most_recent_instance.location.path | startswith("tests/")) | "\(.number) \(.dismissed_reason)"'. ruff and mypy findings fail the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/issues/1258 https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/issues/2427 https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml
static_analysis_often_justification: on every push and pull request: https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/actions/workflows/lint.yml, https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/actions/workflows/codeql.yml
test_branch_coverage80_justification: pyproject.toml sets branch = true in the coverage configuration, so the 100% gate counts branches. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/pyproject.toml
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: test.yml runs the suite on every pull request and every push to main that changes more than root Markdown files or the secrets baseline. A pull request changing only those reports the skip as a pass. Its aggregate job, test: every job passed, is a required check on main. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml
test_justification: 100% coverage floor, enforced locally and in CI: https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/actions/workflows/test.yml
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md makes 100% coverage a gate every change must pass, so new functionality comes with its tests. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-environment-and-the-gates
test_policy_mandated_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires 100% line and branch coverage, and fail_under = 100 fails the CI gate on any new code without a test. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
test_statement_coverage80_justification: pyproject.toml sets fail_under = 100, gated on every pull request by test.yml. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/pyproject.toml
test_statement_coverage90_justification: pyproject.toml sets [tool.coverage.report] fail_under = 100, enforced on every pull request. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/pyproject.toml
tests_are_added_justification: The required check test: every job passed fails any pull request that leaves a line or branch untested. The merged pull requests show recent changes landing with their tests. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents the 100% coverage gate, so new functionality is not accepted without a test. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
two_person_review_justification: Over the last two releases, v2026.11.11 and v2026.11.12, 5 of 88 pull requests were approved by somebody other than the author, 6%, below the 50% the criterion asks (v2026.11.12 2 of 7, v2026.11.11 3 of 81); fametrano gave every one of those approvals. Counted by merge time between release publications, over the same two-release window on every btclib-org project, with gh pr list -R btclib-org/btclib-node -s merged -L 500 -S 'merged:2026-11-12T00:28:10Z..2026-11-12T08:36:22Z' --json author,reviews -q '[.[] | .author.login as $a | [.reviews[] | select(.state == "APPROVED" and .author.login != $a) | .author.login] | unique] | {merged: length, approved: map(select(length > 0)) | length, approvers: (add | unique)}' for v2026.11.12, and the same command over merged:2026-11-07T01:53:14Z..2026-11-12T00:28:09Z for v2026.11.11. main's main-self-merge ruleset requires one approving review from somebody other than the author, and fametrano holds a pull_request-mode bypass of it. Read with gh api repos/btclib-org/btclib-node/rulesets/20736359 --jq '{name, bypass: [.bypass_actors[] | {actor_id, bypass_mode}], reviews: (.rules[] | select(.type == "pull_request") | .parameters | {required_approving_review_count, dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push})}', with admin rights, on 2026-11-12; actor 3296421 is fametrano (gh api users/fametrano --jq .id). https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/2021
updateable_reused_components_justificati: Reused components are either standard-library modules or PyPI packages pinned in uv.lock and bumped weekly by Dependabot, and the deps-latest sentinel runs the full suite against the upgraded set every week. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/.github/workflows/deps-latest.yml
version_semver_justification: Calendar versioning, YYYY.M.D, with the day as the micro level; each release is tagged v<version>. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github#12-releasing
version_tags_signed_justification: Every release tag is signed, and RELEASING.md reads each signature back. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/tags
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No publicly known vulnerability is left unfixed: each published advisory names the release that fixes it. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/security/advisories
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: Every published advisory names the release that fixes it, and no Dependabot alert is open. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/security/advisories
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: An advisory credits its reporter as finder: pmazzocchi on GHSA-rm5x-6v45-j8m6, GHSA-6hv4-mmgr-39wq and GHSA-68jv-ghr4-jjmj. fametrano, the maintainer, filed the others, so they have no outside reporter to credit. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/security/advisories
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: GHSA-rm5x-6v45-j8m6, GHSA-6hv4-mmgr-39wq and GHSA-68jv-ghr4-jjmj, reported privately by pmazzocchi on 2026-09-30, were fixed in v2026.10.4 and published on 2026-10-04. GHSA-74pj-5cgg-3m66 was published with its fix the day it was opened. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/security/advisories
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: SECURITY.md's Reporting a vulnerability gives the private channels (a GitHub security advisory, or security at btclib dot org), who can see a report, and how a CVE is requested. Private vulnerability reporting is enabled. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/SECURITY.md
warnings_fixed_justification: Warnings are not tolerated: ruff, strict mypy and pytest fail the required checks, since pytest's filterwarnings opens with "error" and ignores only named cases. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/pyproject.toml
warnings_justification: mypy strict with all relevant extra checks activated, see https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/pyproject.toml
warnings_strict_justification: ruff runs with `select = ["ALL"]` (every rule family) and mypy runs with `strict = true`; both are required, zero-finding pre-commit hooks enforced again in the lint workflow. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-node/blob/main/pyproject.toml
